about: Provider table for common/deepseek_route.py (the provider-aware guard). A stage declares exactly one provider; the guard forwards only to that provider's base URL with that provider's key. Prices are per 1M tokens, Standard tier, USD. A paid stage refuses any model whose price here is missing or null. Loaded and validated on every run-stage call; receipts of non-DeepSeek runs record this file's sha256.

deepseek.description: Unchanged DeepSeek route. The guard keeps its DeepSeek constants in code (deepseek_route.py: DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL, DEEPSEEK_MODEL, DEEPSEEK_KEY_ENV, PRICE_SNAPSHOT) so DeepSeek behaviour is byte-for-byte what it was at fe2e3e0; this entry mirrors them and run-stage refuses to start if the two disagree.
deepseek.wire: thinking={type: disabled} injected; max_completion_tokens mapped to max_tokens, default and clamp; OpenAI-only fields dropped; developer->system, tool-message name dropped, text blocks joined; embeddings refused unless a stage declares a loopback local_embeddings model

price_snapshot.verification: UNVERIFIED on 2026-10-08 (not re-fetched by this change)

openai.description: OpenAI Chat Completions and Embeddings on the papers' original backbones. The model is never rewritten: each stage lists the exact model ids it may use, and anything else is refused with HTTP 400 before it is sent.
openai.key_file_rule: run-stage and serve read OPENAI_API_KEY only from the --lab-env file, which must be a dedicated file outside every git work tree and not named .env (the lab .env is loaded by load_dotenv in the lab runner and the vendored AgentDojo scripts, and OPENAI_API_KEY is the default credential of the OpenAI SDK and LangChain)

wire.thinking: never added; a request that carries the DeepSeek 'thinking' field is refused
wire.output_limit: max_tokens and max_completion_tokens are both accepted and each is clamped to the stage ceiling; the field(s) used are ledgered as max_tokens_field; if neither is sent the guard adds max_completion_tokens = stage default and ledgers 'default:max_completion_tokens'
wire.logprobs: logprobs and top_logprobs (integer 0-20) pass through unchanged; the ledger records whether the response carried logprobs
wire.service_tier: a request may omit service_tier or send 'default'; any other value is refused. A response whose service_tier is present and not 'default' halts the stage, because these prices are Standard-tier only
refused_fields: message content parts other than text and refusal (image, audio and file parts are billed by rules the pre-flight estimate does not model)
wire.passed_through: everything else, unchanged (no message normalisation, no dropped fields), with two exceptions: when stream is true the guard sets stream_options.include_usage = true (keeping any other stream_options keys) so that every streamed response reports usage; stream_options without stream is removed and ledgered as dropped
wire.upstream_errors: an upstream HTTP 4xx/5xx is ledgered and charged 0 USD; UNVERIFIED that OpenAI never bills one, so the summary counts upstream_error_responses for the dashboard reconciliation (RUN-PLAN-OPENAI.md O13). A stream that breaks before usage arrives is charged at its pre-flight reservation
wire.usage: prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens, completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens; embeddings usage.prompt_tokens (input only)

pricing.tier: Standard (not Batch, Flex, Fast/Priority, Scale; not regional-processing or FedRAMP endpoints)
page_notes: Pricing page: 'Prices per 1M tokens.' 'Short context: <=272K input tokens. Long context: >272K input tokens.' None of the models below lists a long-context or cache-write price (dash).

Pricing page: regional processing (data residency) endpoints carry a 10% uplift for models released on or after 2026-03-05; this guard only talks to https://api.openai.com/v1, and none of these models is that new.
The pricing page gives no page date; the fetch date above is the snapshot date.
pricing.cached_input_policy: cached input tokens (usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens) are charged at cached_input_per_million only where the pricing page lists a cached price for that model; where it is null they are charged as uncached input. Pre-flight reservations always assume no cache hit.

gpt-4.1-mini-2025-04-14.price_basis: pricing page Standard row 'gpt-4.1-mini | $0.40 | $0.10 | - | $1.60'; the gpt-4.1-mini model page lists gpt-4.1-mini-2025-04-14 as its only and default snapshot at input $0.4, cached input $0.1, output $1.6. The dated id itself is not a row of the Standard table (it appears only under fine-tuning).
gpt-4.1-mini-2025-04-14.used_by: attriguard (AttriGuard Table 4 backbone and auxiliary model)

gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18.price_basis: pricing page Standard row 'gpt-4o-mini | $0.15 | $0.075 | - | $0.60'; the gpt-4o-mini model page lists gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18 as its only snapshot at input $0.15, cached input $0.075, output $0.6. The dated id itself is not a row of the Standard table (it appears only under fine-tuning).
gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18.used_by: argus (ARGUS agent and judges), harness Gate H, common S0 key check

gpt-4o-2024-05-13.price_basis: pricing page Standard row 'gpt-4o-2024-05-13 | $5.00 | - | - | $15.00' (its own row; the gpt-4o model page shows $2.5/$1.25/$10 for the default snapshot gpt-4o-2024-08-06, which does not apply here). No cached price is listed, so cached tokens are charged as uncached.
gpt-4o-2024-05-13.used_by: melon (MELON paper GPT-4o rows; agentdojo 0.1.24 ModelsEnum id)

gpt-5.2-2025-12-11.price_basis: pricing page Standard row 'gpt-5.2 | $1.75 | $0.175 | - | $14.00'; the gpt-5.2 model page lists gpt-5.2-2025-12-11 as its default and only snapshot at input $1.75, cached input $0.175, output $14, and calls GPT-5.2 'our previous flagship model' (still listed on 2026-10-08). Reasoning tokens are billed as output.

text-embedding-3-large.price_basis: pricing page Specialized models 'Embedding | text-embedding-3-large | $0.13 | - | -'; the model page lists text-embedding-3-large as its only snapshot at $0.13 per 1M tokens. Input tokens only.
text-embedding-3-large.used_by: melon (MELON detection embedder, pi_detector.py hard-codes this id)

not_in_table.gpt-4o-mini, gpt-4.1-mini, gpt-4o, gpt-5: floating aliases are deliberately absent: a stage may only allow dated snapshot ids, so an alias request is refused
not_in_table.gpt-5.5: PAA's second reference backbone; Standard row 'gpt-5.5 (<272K context length) | $5.00 | $0.50 | - | $30.00' on 2026-10-08. Not added: PAA reaches it through the Codex CLI, which the guard cannot meter (RUN-PLAN-OPENAI.md section 9).

groq.description: Groq synchronous on-demand Chat Completions for the constructed A1 G1 second-backbone screen. Only openai/gpt-oss-120b is allowed; the exact model ID is never rewritten.
groq.key_file_rule: run-stage and serve read GROQ_API_KEY only from a dedicated --lab-env key file outside every git work tree and not named .env. The key is held by the parent guard only; the child receives a loopback guard token and a scrubbed environment.
groq.wire: Groq GPT-OSS-120B only; no model rewrite, thinking field, embeddings, logprobs, n>1, or messages[].name. The guard preserves max_completion_tokens and reasoning_effort=low and bounds completion tokens. Omitted service_tier selects Groq on_demand; auto, flex and performance are refused.

pricing.cached_input_policy: Pre-flight reserves at the uncached input price. Usage prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens is charged at the model page's cached input price; missing cache detail is charged as uncached.

openai/gpt-oss-120b.price_basis: Groq official GPT OSS 120B model page, fetched 2026-10-10: input $0.15, cached input $0.075, output $0.60 per 1M tokens. Groq service-tiers page says omitted service_tier is on_demand.
openai/gpt-oss-120b.used_by: constructed A1 G1 Groq model screen only
